sections.label: WARNING
sections.text: MetMalaysia issued a thunderstorm warning at 12:00 today for Sabah's West Coast division, which includes Kota Kinabalu, together with Interior, Kudat, Sandakan and Tawau areas: thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 15:00 MYT. The warnings card shows whether it is still in force.

sections.label: TODAY
sections.text: Hot and bright so far: the airport measured 32°C with a few low clouds at 12:30, and the blended model put the feels-like temperature at 38°C at 12:00. Thunderstorms this afternoon are likely. The KK airport forecast (TAF) has temporary thunderstorm rain during 15:00–19:00 MYT; MetMalaysia's town forecast says thunderstorms this afternoon and no rain tonight (the district forecast says 'in a few places'); the blended model's rain chance jumps from 45% at 12:00 to 77% at 13:00 and 98–100% at 14:00–15:00, easing to 52% by 18:00 and 22% by 19:00. So the first cells can arrive before the TAF period. Today's model highs run 28.9–33.4°C (median 30.9°C); MetMalaysia gives 32°C town / 33°C district and the airport is already at 32°C, so I favour 32–33°C before the storms knock it back.

sections.label: RAIN AMOUNT
sections.text: The ECMWF ensemble is light for today at the airport grid point: 10th–90th percentile 1.4–7.4 mm, only a 4% chance of 10 mm or more. Yesterday's storm (active 14:13–18:00 at the airport) shows what 'light' can still mean under a cell: amounts are grid-point daily totals, not what falls on one street.

sections.label: THIS WEEK
sections.text: Dry mornings and afternoon thunderstorms every day, with the wet focus now on Tuesday 10 and Wednesday 11 Nov: the ensemble's chance of a 10 mm+ day is 4% today, 10% Monday, then 47% Tuesday and 41% Wednesday (likely 3.8–19.3 mm and 3.9–18.1 mm), easing to 35% Thursday and 22% Friday–Saturday. MetMalaysia keeps 'thunderstorms in a few places' each afternoon through Tuesday and adds rain on Monday night. Highs 32–33°C, lows 24–25°C. Separately, the continuous-rain alert for Kudat and the Sandakan areas runs to Wednesday 11 Nov; it does not name Kota Kinabalu.

sections.label: PLAN
sections.text: This call was first written at 12:55 and amended at 13:11 MYT; the morning's 'finish outdoor work by 13:00' advice has passed. From now: stay under cover through the afternoon, with the West Coast land thunderstorm warning in force until 15:00 and the airport's thunderstorm period 15:00–19:00; the evening and night look dry (town forecast: no rain). Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons are the ones most likely to disrupt site visits or driving this week. The separate coastal thunderstorm warning for Eastern Sabah waters expired at 13:00; check the warnings card for anything newer before going to sea.

sections.label: CONFIDENCE
sections.text: Temperature: high (already measured at 32°C, official forecast agrees). Timing of today's storms: moderate to high (TAF, MetMalaysia and the model peak all point to mid-afternoon; exact local timing stays uncertain). Rain amount at your spot: low. The Tuesday–Wednesday wet signal: moderate, from one ensemble two to three days out.

sections.label: WHY
sections.text: Forecasts made 24 hours ahead were checked against yesterday's airport readings: GFS (1.6°C error) and ECMWF (1.6°C) led, the blend 1.8°C, UK Met Office 2.4°C, JMA 2.6°C, GEM 2.7°C, ICON and CMA 3.1°C, ARPEGE 3.2°C; GEM, ICON and CMA ran 2.2–2.5°C too warm. GFS, ECMWF, the blend, JMA, GEM and ICON predicted rain in the 14:00–18:00 window; UK Met Office, CMA and ARPEGE did not, and a thunderstorm was in fact reported 14:13–18:00. Two days of comparison now, still a small sample; it informs my grouping of the models and no weights are computed. No radar check was made for this call.
